svg.title: Outgoing CTA roles for Direct and hierarchical sending
svg.desc: Capacity 512, 384 physical CTAs, 256 logical RDMA send CTAs. A Direct rank sending 16 tokens uses CTAs 0 to 15 for RDMA and CTAs 368 to 383 for overlapping local LSA forwarding. A hierarchical rank sending 256 tokens uses CTAs 0 to 255 for RDMA and defers local forwarding until after the prefix grid barrier. These are temporary send-phase roles.
svg.text: Prioritize RDMA; overlap local forwarding when workers are available.
Tuned capacity-512 preset: 384 physical CTAs · 256 logical RDMA send CTAs
Direct · 16 tokens → 16 RDMA producers + 16 local-copy producers
CTAs 0–15
Stage + post RDMA
One token per send CTA
CTAs 16–367
No outgoing payload in this phase
Still participate in later clearing, synchronization, and receive work
Forward over local LSA
Independent local headers
Front and back producer ranges run independently; neither consumes the other’s staging.
Hierarchical · 256 tokens → 256 RDMA producers; local workers reused later
CTAs 0–255
Stage + post one copy per required remote domain
Local LSA forwarding follows remote submission and the prefix grid join
No outgoing payload in this phase
These CTAs take on later work
Active RDMA producers = max(1, min(256, N)); producer i handles tokens i, i + 256, …
Stage and submit remote traffic first: it starts the network hop and remote forwarding chain.
512 tokens still use 256 RDMA producers, with two tokens each. The total launch remains 384 CTAs.
Tuned counts, not protocol requirements. Ranges are not to scale. Receive ownership is assigned later.
